html:
The sample sorter is the first scene most people open: File → New Project → Sandbox: sample sorter scene. An emitter drops cartons and the odd metal box onto two belts; an entry eye, an inductive prox, a pusher over a bin, a colour sensor, a pivot arm over a second bin and a remover at the end; a panel with Start, Stop, an E-stop, a HAND / AUTO selector, a stack light with a buzzer, a fault lamp, a count display and a speed pot; and a wash tank with its floats and a mixer. It has always come with no logic. it has a reference program (File → Load Reference Solution: Sample sorter) and a guided track (File → New Project → Guided: sample sorter, or Guided → Guide This Scene: the Sample Sorter on the plain scene). This chapter is that program, in the order a sorting line is commissioned: make it run and stop, feed it, count it, sort it, protect it.

The tags

Every signal gets an alias named Device_Signal, which is what Alias all I/O in the scene’s properties makes, so PB_Stop_Pressed is the Stop button’s contact and Pusher_Metal_Extended the pusher’s front reed switch. The guided project makes them for you. The program’s own tags:

TagTypeDescription
RunBOOLThe line is running: Start sealed in, Stop and the E-stop healthy, no bin full
Feed_msDINTTime between parts in AUTO, from the speed pot: 2000 + 40 x pot (2 to 6 s)
T_FeedTIMERFeed interval timer; its ACC is compared with Feed_ms
Feed_PulseBOOLOne scan: release a part (AUTO)
TagTypeDescription
Hand_ONSBOOLOne-shot storage for the HAND release
Hand_FeedBOOLOne scan: release a part (HAND, on a Start press)
Entry_ONSBOOLOne-shot storage for the entry count
Out_ONSBOOLOne-shot storage for the pass-through count
Parts_InDINTParts seen by PE_Entry, shown on Disp_Count
Parts_OutDINTParts that reached the remover unsorted
Metal_SeenBOOLA metal part has passed Prox_Metal and is on its way to the pusher
Red_SeenBOOLA red part has passed Color_1 and is on its way to the arm
Red_At_ArmBOOLThat red part has reached the arm’s eye
T_ArmTIMERThe arm stays in the lane 1 s after the red part leaves its eye
Bin_FullBOOLEither bin is full: the line stops until it is emptied
T_BuzzTIMERThe buzzer sounds for the first 5 s of a bin-full stop

The index

Like the elevator and the intersection, the main routine is a table of contents: one JSR per job, Init only on the first scan.

Start and stop

The feed

The emitter releases a part on a rising edge of Emit, and only while its exit is clear (PartReady). In HAND each Start press releases one part; in AUTO a timer releases one every Feed_ms, which the pot sets between two and six seconds. The timer’s preset is a ceiling, not the interval: the interval is the GEQ on its accumulator, which is how you get a timer whose time comes from an analog input without writing to .PRE.

Count

Sort the metal

The prox is upstream of the pusher, so the program has to remember what it saw for the hundred pixels between them. One latch is a tracking register one part long, and it is enough because at the fastest feed the parts are two seconds apart and the belt covers prox-to-pusher in under one. The day the parts come closer than the sensor is to the actuator, the latch becomes a shift register (Part IV’s Track routine does exactly that).

Sort the red

A pusher fires when the part is in front of it; an arm has to be across the lane before the part gets there. So the arm swings as soon as red is seen and comes back a second after the part has left its eye.

The alarms and the stack light

A full bin stops the line through the XIO in the seal-in; click the bin to empty it (in a sandbox scene a click on a bin empties it and the log says so; a level’s bins are its score and do not) and press Start.

The wash tank

Guided: the sample sorter

Nine lessons, one routine each, in the order above: Init, Run_Stop (Start seals in and lights the button; Stop drops it), Feed (a part per press in HAND, then AUTO), Count (Parts_In on the display), Sort_Metal (a metal box in its bin, the pusher back), Sort_Red (a red box in its bin, the arm back), Alarms (green running; the E-stop gives red and the fault lamp), Tank (the inlet fills, the mixer turns) and Ready. The reference rungs come hints first, as everywhere in guided mode: the comment, then what the rung uses, then its shape, then the text.

Try it: break the tracking

Turn the pot to 0 (two seconds between parts) and, in Program mode, drag Prox_Metal back towards the emitter until it is further from the pusher than two parts are from each other. Run: a metal box followed closely by a carton fires the pusher at the carton. Then replace Metal_Seen with a BSL on a DINT, clocked by the entry eye, and read the bit for the pusher’s position. That is the step from a latch to a tracking register, and the reason Part IV is built the way it is.

Machine faults on the sample sorter

Tools → Inject Machine Fault… lists the faults that belong to the parts on this floor. Each has a fault card: the symptom, what to watch in the I/O to confirm it, the repair, and what a program should do about it. Repair on an active fault removes its cause the way a technician would; whether the machine runs again is up to the program. The sorter also has the belts’ and the eyes’ faults (a jam, an overload, a dirty lens).

FaultWatchRepairThe program should

Try it: a stroke-time alarm

Inject Pusher: extended reed switch dead with the reference running: the pusher goes out and stays commanded out for ever, because nothing in Sort_Metal ever times the stroke. Add the rung a real machine has, XIC(Pusher_Metal_Extend)XIO(Pusher_Metal_Extended)TON(T_Stroke,1000,0), put XIC(T_Stroke.DN) into the fault lamp and the Run seal, and inject it again. The same rung catches Air lost. That is the whole idea of fault handling: time what you commanded against what you were told happened.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE INDEX. Init once on the first scan; then every scan: run and stop, the feed, the counts, the two sorts, the alarms and the tank
rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung runs the routine Init.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. JSR(Init) Jump to Subroutine does: runs the routine Init. The routine is scanned at this point, then the scan comes back here.

pats.t: Part of the index: one call, one job.
pats.why: The main routine calls each routine in turn. A routine that is not called is not scanned, however correct its rungs are.
pats.think: a running order on a clipboard: the main routine reads it top to bottom, and each line sends you to a page that does one job.
pats.watch: A new routine does nothing until a JSR calls it. If a routine’s rungs never highlight online, look here first.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung runs the routine Run_Stop.
rungs.ltr: 1. JSR(Run_Stop) Jump to Subroutine does: runs the routine Run_Stop. The routine is scanned at this point, then the scan comes back here.

pats.t: Part of the index: one call, one job.

rungs.head: Init · Rung 0
rungs.comment: FIRST SCAN: forget any part the program thought it was tracking (the belt may have been cleared while it was stopped), pull the pusher back, zero the counts

pred.q: S:FS is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Metal_Seen is unlatched, Red_Seen is unlatched, Red_At_Arm is unlatched, Pusher_Metal_Extend is unlatched, Parts_In is written and Parts_Out is written.

rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung unlatches Metal_Seen (A metal part has passed Prox_Metal and is on its way to the pusher), unlatches Red_Seen (A red part has passed Color_1 and is on its way to the arm), unlatches Red_At_Arm (That red part has reached the arm's eye), unlatches Pusher_Metal_Extend (Pusher_Metal Extend: Solenoid: extend cylinder), clears Parts_In (Parts seen by PE_Entry, shown on Disp_Count) to 0 and clears Parts_Out (Parts that reached the remover unsorted) to 0.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Metal_Seen) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Metal_Seen. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Red_Seen) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Red_Seen. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Red_At_Arm) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Red_At_Arm. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTU(Pusher_Metal_Extend) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Pusher_Metal_Extend. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 5
    1. CLR(Parts_In) Clear does: clears Parts_In to 0.
    Path 6
    1. CLR(Parts_Out) Clear does: clears Parts_Out to 0.

pats.t: An unlatch.
pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Metal_Seen when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Run_Stop · Rung 0
rungs.comment: START / STOP: the seal-in. Start makes Run, Run holds itself; the Stop button is wired normally closed (1 until pressed) and so is the E-stop, so both are XIC. A full bin breaks the seal too: the line stops rather than spill

pred.q: PB_Start_Pressed is on, Run is off, PB_Stop_Pressed is off, EStop_1_OK is on and Bin_Full is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Run is off. It stops at XIC(PB_Stop_Pressed).

rungs.words: When either (PB_Start_Pressed (PB_Start Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on) or (Run (The line is running: Start sealed in, Stop and the E-stop healthy, no bin full) is on), PB_Stop_Pressed (PB_Stop Pressed: NC contact: 1 until pressed) is on, EStop_1_OK (EStop_1 OK: NC contact: 1 while healthy, 0 when pressed) is on and Bin_Full (Either bin is full: the line stops until it is emptied) is off, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(PB_Start_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when PB_Start_Pressed is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(PB_Stop_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when PB_Stop_Pressed is on.
  3. XIC(EStop_1_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when EStop_1_OK is on.
  4. XIO(Bin_Full) Examine If Open asks: true when Bin_Full is off.
  5. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: Seal-in.
pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Run_Stop · Rung 1
rungs.comment: Both belts and the lamp in the Start button follow Run
rungs.words: When Run (The line is running: Start sealed in, Stop and the E-stop healthy, no bin full) is on, the rung turns Belt_1_Fwd (Belt_1 Fwd: Motor forward) on (and off whenever the rung is false), turns Belt_2_Fwd (Belt_2 Fwd: Motor forward) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns PB_Start_Lamp (PB_Start Lamp: Button lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Belt_1_Fwd) Output Energize does: turns Belt_1_Fwd on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Belt_2_Fwd) Output Energize does: turns Belt_2_Fwd on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 3
    1. OTE(PB_Start_Lamp) Output Energize does: turns PB_Start_Lamp on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Feed · Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE FEED RATE from the speed pot (0 to 100): 2 s between parts at 0, 6 s at 100. The branch runs top to bottom, so the ADD sees the MUL's result
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung makes Feed_ms (Time between parts in AUTO, from the speed pot: 2000 + 40 x pot (2 to 6 s)) = Pot_Speed_Value (Pot_Speed Value: 0-100) × 40 and makes Feed_ms = Feed_ms + 2000.
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MUL(Pot_Speed_Value,40,Feed_ms) Multiply does: makes Feed_ms = Pot_Speed_Value × 40.
    Path 2
    1. ADD(Feed_ms,2000,Feed_ms) Add does: makes Feed_ms = Feed_ms + 2000. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

rungs.head: Feed · Rung 1
rungs.comment: AUTO (selector right): a timer that runs until the next release. Its preset is only a ceiling; the interval is the compare below

pred.q: Run is on, Sel_Auto_Pos2 is on and Feed_Pulse is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: T_Feed times toward its preset.

rungs.words: When Run (The line is running: Start sealed in, Stop and the E-stop healthy, no bin full) is on, Sel_Auto_Pos2 (Sel_Auto Pos2: 1 in the right-hand position) is on and Feed_Pulse (One scan: release a part (AUTO)) is off, the rung runs the timer T_Feed (Feed interval timer; its ACC is compared with Feed_ms) toward 60000 ms (60 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Sel_Auto_Pos2) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sel_Auto_Pos2 is on.
  3. XIO(Feed_Pulse) Examine If Open asks: true when Feed_Pulse is off.
  4. TON(T_Feed,60000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_Feed toward 60000 ms (60 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_Feed counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Feed · Rung 2
rungs.comment: When the timer has run Feed_ms, one scan of Feed_Pulse; that same bit resets the timer on the next scan through the XIO above

pred.q: Run is off, T_Feed.ACC is 48 and Feed_ms is 17. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Feed_Pulse is off. It stops at XIC(Run).

rungs.words: When Run (The line is running: Start sealed in, Stop and the E-stop healthy, no bin full) is on and T_Feed.ACC (the accumulated value of T_Feed: Feed interval timer; its ACC is compared with Feed_ms) is at least Feed_ms (Time between parts in AUTO, from the speed pot: 2000 + 40 x pot (2 to 6 s)), the rung turns Feed_Pulse (One scan: release a part (AUTO)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. GEQ(T_Feed.ACC,Feed_ms) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when T_Feed.ACC is at least Feed_ms.
  3. OTE(Feed_Pulse) Output Energize does: turns Feed_Pulse on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Feed · Rung 3
rungs.comment: HAND (selector left): one part for each press of Start
rungs.words: When Run (The line is running: Start sealed in, Stop and the E-stop healthy, no bin full) is on, Sel_Auto_Pos2 (Sel_Auto Pos2: 1 in the right-hand position) is off, PB_Start_Pressed (PB_Start Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Hand_Feed (One scan: release a part (HAND, on a Start press)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Sel_Auto_Pos2) Examine If Open asks: true when Sel_Auto_Pos2 is off.
  3. XIC(PB_Start_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when PB_Start_Pressed is on.
  4. ONS(Hand_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Hand_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  5. OTE(Hand_Feed) Output Energize does: turns Hand_Feed on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Feed · Rung 4
rungs.comment: Release a part, only if the emitter's exit is clear. The emitter fires on the rising edge, so a one-scan pulse is one part

pred.q: Feed_Pulse is on, Hand_Feed is on and Emitter_1_PartReady is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Emitter_1_Emit is on.

rungs.words: When either (Feed_Pulse (One scan: release a part (AUTO)) is on) or (Hand_Feed (One scan: release a part (HAND, on a Start press)) is on) and Emitter_1_PartReady (Emitter_1 PartReady: Exit clear, ready to emit) is on, the rung turns Emitter_1_Emit (Emitter_1 Emit: Release a part (rising edge, or continuous while on)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Feed_Pulse) Examine If Closed asks: true when Feed_Pulse is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Hand_Feed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hand_Feed is on.
  2. XIC(Emitter_1_PartReady) Examine If Closed asks: true when Emitter_1_PartReady is on.
  3. OTE(Emitter_1_Emit) Output Energize does: turns Emitter_1_Emit on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Count · Rung 0
rungs.comment: COUNT what comes in: once per part, on the eye's rising edge
rungs.words: When PE_Entry_Detect (PE_Entry Detect: Detecting: a solid part is within range) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung makes Parts_In (Parts seen by PE_Entry, shown on Disp_Count) = Parts_In + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Entry_Detect) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Entry_Detect is on.
  2. ONS(Entry_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Entry_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. ADD(Parts_In,1,Parts_In) Add does: makes Parts_In = Parts_In + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Count · Rung 1
rungs.comment: …and what goes out at the end unsorted
rungs.words: When Remover_1_Detect (Remover_1 Detect: Part entering the remover) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung makes Parts_Out (Parts that reached the remover unsorted) = Parts_Out + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Remover_1_Detect) Examine If Closed asks: true when Remover_1_Detect is on.
  2. ONS(Out_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Out_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. ADD(Parts_Out,1,Parts_Out) Add does: makes Parts_Out = Parts_Out + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Count · Rung 2
rungs.comment: The display on the panel shows Parts_In
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung puts Parts_In (Parts seen by PE_Entry, shown on Disp_Count) into Disp_Count_Value (Disp_Count Value: Number to show).
rungs.ltr: 1. MOV(Parts_In,Disp_Count_Value) Move does: puts Parts_In into Disp_Count_Value. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Sort_Metal · Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE METAL SORT. The inductive prox sees only metal; it is upstream of the pusher, so remember what it saw: one latch is a tracking register one part long, enough while the parts are further apart than prox and pusher

pred.q: Prox_Metal_Detect is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Metal_Seen is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Prox_Metal_Detect).

rungs.words: When Prox_Metal_Detect (Prox_Metal Detect: Detecting: a conductive (metal) part is within range) is on, the rung latches Metal_Seen (A metal part has passed Prox_Metal and is on its way to the pusher) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Prox_Metal_Detect) Examine If Closed asks: true when Prox_Metal_Detect is on.
  2. OTL(Metal_Seen) Output Latch does: latches Metal_Seen on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.t: A latch.
pats.why: Metal_Seen stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: Sort_Metal · Rung 1
rungs.comment: The part reaches the eye in front of the pusher: fire
rungs.words: When Metal_Seen (A metal part has passed Prox_Metal and is on its way to the pusher) is on and Pusher_Metal_Detect (Pusher_Metal Detect: Photoeye in front of the pusher) is on, the rung latches Pusher_Metal_Extend (Pusher_Metal Extend: Solenoid: extend cylinder) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Metal_Seen) Examine If Closed asks: true when Metal_Seen is on.
  2. XIC(Pusher_Metal_Detect) Examine If Closed asks: true when Pusher_Metal_Detect is on.
  3. OTL(Pusher_Metal_Extend) Output Latch does: latches Pusher_Metal_Extend on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.t: A latch.
pats.why: Pusher_Metal_Extend stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Sort_Metal · Rung 2
rungs.comment: At full stroke (the reed switch), retract and forget the part: it is in the bin

pred.q: Pusher_Metal_Extended is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Pusher_Metal_Extend is unlatched and Metal_Seen is unlatched.

rungs.words: When Pusher_Metal_Extended (Pusher_Metal Extended: Reed switch: cylinder extended) is on, the rung unlatches Pusher_Metal_Extend (Pusher_Metal Extend: Solenoid: extend cylinder) and unlatches Metal_Seen (A metal part has passed Prox_Metal and is on its way to the pusher).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Pusher_Metal_Extended) Examine If Closed asks: true when Pusher_Metal_Extended is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Pusher_Metal_Extend) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Pusher_Metal_Extend. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Metal_Seen) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Metal_Seen. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.t: An unlatch.
pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Pusher_Metal_Extend when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Sort_Red · Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE RED SORT. The colour sensor's red bank; remember it

pred.q: Color_1_Red is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Red_Seen is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Color_1_Red).

rungs.words: When Color_1_Red (Color_1 Red: Bank 1: red) is on, the rung latches Red_Seen (A red part has passed Color_1 and is on its way to the arm) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Color_1_Red) Examine If Closed asks: true when Color_1_Red is on.
  2. OTL(Red_Seen) Output Latch does: latches Red_Seen on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.t: A latch.
pats.why: Red_Seen stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Sort_Red · Rung 1
rungs.comment: The arm swings into the lane as soon as a red part is on its way, so it is across the belt before the part gets there
rungs.words: When Red_Seen (A red part has passed Color_1 and is on its way to the arm) is on, the rung turns Arm_Red_Turn (Arm_Red Turn: Swing the arm into the lane) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Red_Seen) Examine If Closed asks: true when Red_Seen is on.
  2. OTE(Arm_Red_Turn) Output Energize does: turns Arm_Red_Turn on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Sort_Red · Rung 2
rungs.comment: The red part reaches the arm's eye…

pred.q: Red_Seen is on and Arm_Red_Detect is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Red_At_Arm latches on.

rungs.words: When Red_Seen (A red part has passed Color_1 and is on its way to the arm) is on and Arm_Red_Detect (Arm_Red Detect: Photoeye ahead of the arm) is on, the rung latches Red_At_Arm (That red part has reached the arm's eye) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Red_Seen) Examine If Closed asks: true when Red_Seen is on.
  2. XIC(Arm_Red_Detect) Examine If Closed asks: true when Arm_Red_Detect is on.
  3. OTL(Red_At_Arm) Output Latch does: latches Red_At_Arm on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.t: A latch.
pats.why: Red_At_Arm stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Sort_Red · Rung 3
rungs.comment: …and leaves it, guided along the arm into the bin; give it a second
rungs.words: When Red_At_Arm (That red part has reached the arm's eye) is on and Arm_Red_Detect (Arm_Red Detect: Photoeye ahead of the arm) is off, the rung runs the timer T_Arm (The arm stays in the lane 1 s after the red part leaves its eye) toward 1000 ms (1 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Red_At_Arm) Examine If Closed asks: true when Red_At_Arm is on.
  2. XIO(Arm_Red_Detect) Examine If Open asks: true when Arm_Red_Detect is off.
  3. TON(T_Arm,1000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_Arm toward 1000 ms (1 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_Arm counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Sort_Red · Rung 4
rungs.comment: Then the arm comes back out of the lane

pred.q: T_Arm.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Red_Seen is left as it was and Red_At_Arm is left as it was. It stops at XIC(T_Arm.DN).

rungs.words: When T_Arm.DN (the done bit of T_Arm: The arm stays in the lane 1 s after the red part leaves its eye) is on, the rung unlatches Red_Seen (A red part has passed Color_1 and is on its way to the arm) and unlatches Red_At_Arm (That red part has reached the arm's eye).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_Arm.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_Arm.DN is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Red_Seen) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Red_Seen. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Red_At_Arm) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Red_At_Arm. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.t: An unlatch.
pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Red_Seen when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 0
rungs.comment: A FULL BIN stops the line (Run_Stop has XIO(Bin_Full)); click the bin to empty it, then Start

pred.q: Bin_Metal_Full is off and Bin_Red_Full is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Bin_Full is on.

rungs.words: When either (Bin_Metal_Full (Bin_Metal Full: Bin holds its capacity) is on) or (Bin_Red_Full (Bin_Red Full: Bin holds its capacity) is on), the rung turns Bin_Full (Either bin is full: the line stops until it is emptied) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Bin_Metal_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Bin_Metal_Full is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Bin_Red_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Bin_Red_Full is on.
  2. OTE(Bin_Full) Output Energize does: turns Bin_Full on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 1
rungs.comment: THE STACK LIGHT: green running
rungs.words: When Run (The line is running: Start sealed in, Stop and the E-stop healthy, no bin full) is on, the rung turns Stack_1_Green (Stack_1 Green: Green segment) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. OTE(Stack_1_Green) Output Energize does: turns Stack_1_Green on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 2
rungs.comment: amber: a bin wants emptying

pred.q: Bin_Full is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Stack_1_Amber is off. It stops at XIC(Bin_Full).

rungs.words: When Bin_Full (Either bin is full: the line stops until it is emptied) is on, the rung turns Stack_1_Amber (Stack_1 Amber: Amber segment) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Bin_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Bin_Full is on.
  2. OTE(Stack_1_Amber) Output Energize does: turns Stack_1_Amber on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 3
rungs.comment: red, and the fault lamp: the E-stop is pressed
rungs.words: When EStop_1_OK (EStop_1 OK: NC contact: 1 while healthy, 0 when pressed) is off, the rung turns Stack_1_Red (Stack_1 Red: Red segment) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Lamp_Fault_On (Lamp_Fault On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(EStop_1_OK) Examine If Open asks: true when EStop_1_OK is off.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Stack_1_Red) Output Energize does: turns Stack_1_Red on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Lamp_Fault_On) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 4
rungs.comment: The buzzer calls somebody for the first five seconds of a bin-full stop, then lets the amber do the talking

pred.q: Bin_Full is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: T_Buzz times toward its preset.

rungs.words: When Bin_Full (Either bin is full: the line stops until it is emptied) is on, the rung runs the timer T_Buzz (The buzzer sounds for the first 5 s of a bin-full stop) toward 5000 ms (5 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Bin_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Bin_Full is on.
  2. TON(T_Buzz,5000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_Buzz toward 5000 ms (5 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_Buzz counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 5
rungs.words: When Bin_Full (Either bin is full: the line stops until it is emptied) is on and T_Buzz.DN (the done bit of T_Buzz: The buzzer sounds for the first 5 s of a bin-full stop) is off, the rung turns Stack_1_Buzzer (Stack_1 Buzzer: Buzzer) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Bin_Full) Examine If Closed asks: true when Bin_Full is on.
  2. XIO(T_Buzz.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when T_Buzz.DN is off.
  3. OTE(Stack_1_Buzzer) Output Energize does: turns Stack_1_Buzzer on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Tank · Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE WASH TANK beside the line. Fill between the floats: LowFloat is 1 when the level is down at the low float, HighFloat 1 when it is up at the high one. The inlet opens at the low float and seals itself in until the high float makes. Two floats and a seal-in is the oldest level control there is

pred.q: Tank_1_HighFloat is off, Tank_1_LowFloat is off and Tank_1_Inlet is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Tank_1_Inlet is off. None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: When Tank_1_HighFloat (Tank_1 HighFloat: High level float switch) is off and either (Tank_1_LowFloat (Tank_1 LowFloat: Low level float switch) is on) or (Tank_1_Inlet (Tank_1 Inlet: Inlet valve) is on), the rung turns Tank_1_Inlet on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Tank_1_HighFloat) Examine If Open asks: true when Tank_1_HighFloat is off.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Tank_1_LowFloat) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tank_1_LowFloat is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Tank_1_Inlet) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tank_1_Inlet is on.
  3. OTE(Tank_1_Inlet) Output Energize does: turns Tank_1_Inlet on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: Seal-in.
pats.why: The start condition turns Tank_1_Inlet on, and Tank_1_Inlet’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.

rungs.head: Tank · Rung 1
rungs.comment: The line draws from the tank while it runs, never below the low float
rungs.words: When Run (The line is running: Start sealed in, Stop and the E-stop healthy, no bin full) is on and Tank_1_LowFloat (Tank_1 LowFloat: Low level float switch) is off, the rung turns Tank_1_Outlet (Tank_1 Outlet: Outlet valve) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Tank_1_LowFloat) Examine If Open asks: true when Tank_1_LowFloat is off.
  3. OTE(Tank_1_Outlet) Output Energize does: turns Tank_1_Outlet on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Tank · Rung 2
rungs.comment: The mixer runs with the line, and only with its blades covered (above 20 %)

pred.q: Run is on and Tank_1_Level is 21. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Tank_1_Mixer is on.

rungs.words: When Run (The line is running: Start sealed in, Stop and the E-stop healthy, no bin full) is on and Tank_1_Level (Tank_1 Level: Level 0-100 % (bind it to a REAL tag for the unrounded value)) is greater than 20, the rung turns Tank_1_Mixer (Tank_1 Mixer: Mixer motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. GRT(Tank_1_Level,20) Greater Than asks: true when Tank_1_Level is greater than 20.
  3. OTE(Tank_1_Mixer) Output Energize does: turns Tank_1_Mixer on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

Hand_Feed.desc: One scan: release a part (HAND, on a Start press)

Emitter_1_PartReady.desc: Emitter_1 PartReady: Exit clear, ready to emit

Emitter_1_Emit.desc: Emitter_1 Emit: Release a part (rising edge, or continuous while on)

PE_Entry_Detect.desc: PE_Entry Detect: Detecting: a solid part is within range

Remover_1_Detect.desc: Remover_1 Detect: Part entering the remover

Out_ONS.desc: One-shot storage for the pass-through count

Prox_Metal_Detect.desc: Prox_Metal Detect: Detecting: a conductive (metal) part is within range

Pusher_Metal_Detect.desc: Pusher_Metal Detect: Photoeye in front of the pusher

Pusher_Metal_Extended.desc: Pusher_Metal Extended: Reed switch: cylinder extended

Arm_Red_Turn.desc: Arm_Red Turn: Swing the arm into the lane

Arm_Red_Detect.desc: Arm_Red Detect: Photoeye ahead of the arm

Bin_Metal_Full.desc: Bin_Metal Full: Bin holds its capacity

Bin_Red_Full.desc: Bin_Red Full: Bin holds its capacity
